name: pixling
summary: Art know-how and tools for coding agents: pipelines, styles (with how they were made) and taste for making game sprites with code.

install.cmd: git clone https://github.com/trinity-works/pixling && cd pixling && pip install -e .

items.name: spec
items.makes: 8-direction pixel sprites, props, buildings from a JSON spec
items.entry: pixling new EXAMPLE NAME; pixling build SPEC

items.name: blocks
items.makes: small iso units and creatures from a few voxel layers, 4 rotated facings, cast shadows

items.name: iso
items.makes: exact 2:1 isometric scenes and animal sheets from a Python kit

items.name: map
items.makes: living maps: building states, hour light, meaning layer, engine layers

items.name: fx
items.makes: VFX sheets posterised to a style ramp

items.name: video
items.makes: sprites cut from AI video: start sheet -> MiniMax H3 takes -> keyed 8-direction sheets

items.name: strike
items.makes: melee hits that land where the art paints them: weapon, feet and hurtbox per frame of any sprite sheet; the melee range the art supports
items.entry: pixling strike pose SHEET --cell C --pivot X,Y --rows se,.. --hit N; pixling strike reach ATTACK.pose.json IDLE.pose.json --scale K --ppm P --stop M

items.name: painted
items.makes: painterly (non-pixel) sprites, a composed scene and a walkable web scene
items.entry: pixling painted kit; pixling painted compose

items.name: fp
items.makes: a walkable pixel world: a painted scene in layers (Blender painted cards at screen resolution with crisp pixel actors; pixel and flat looks one button away) with a small walker (opens), or first person in WebGL
items.engine: fp (canvas 2D painted layers; WebGL, three.js for first person)
needs: Blender or a python with bpy (re-painting the layers only)
items.entry: pixling fp layers; pixling fp serve; pixling fp bundle

items.name: arena
items.makes: painted battle maps for your own units with a complete, checked game level (collision, nav, LOS, zones); two maps ship: Hushfall Crossing and Emberleaf Hollow
items.engine: arena (Blender data passes, Python painter, canvas 2D viewer)
needs: Blender or a python with bpy (re-painting only)
items.entry: pixling arena maps; pixling arena bundle; pixling arena export; pixling arena check

items.name: style
items.makes: a new art style: refs -> DNA -> hand -> kit -> brief -> review card -> walk -> vote

loop: edit the spec and repeat until it reads well at 1x

commands.does: the pipelines: what each makes, when to pick it, steps, code, lessons
how a launch style was made: hand, kit code, lab notes, build command

commands.cmd: pixling world tactics|flat [--only SCENE] [--frames N] [--out DIR]
commands.does: build a style's scenes and animal sheets with its kit
docs and research notes by topic and section; --grep WORD searches them
styles, materials and ramps
example specs to copy
engine and style-kit modules with docstrings and file paths (pixling code tactics.kit)
copy an example spec

commands.cmd: pixling build SPEC [--clips C] [--dirs D] [--out DIR]
commands.does: render sheets, GIFs and JSON
zoomed review sheet (PNG) to look at
assets side by side at game scale
numeric hints
pixel cleanliness of a 1x render: orphans, whiskers, broken stairs
bone and material maps
versions side by side

commands.cmd: pixling fx KIND --style S [--ramp R] [--param k=v]
commands.does: standalone VFX sheet
compose a map; layers and meaning for engines
building states
map at every hour plus light.json
itch.io-ready pack
editable .aseprite file
setup checks
skill + AGENTS.md block for a project
AI images/video/3D/audio via Scenario (the video pipeline); login must be run by the user
painterly non-pixel pipeline via Blender (experimental)
pixel worlds you walk: a painted layered view with a small walker (opens), and a first-person WebGL walk; screenshots and films through the real runtime
painted battle maps: the viewer as one html, level.json for your units, fairness and walkability checks, zone-budget lint; --map NAME
video pipeline: start frames, take checks, chroma key, cut to sheets, review page, demo, additive spell sheets

commands.cmd: pixling strike pose SHEET.png --cell C --pivot X,Y --rows R [--hit N] [--walk] [--parts MAP.png] | NAME.json --clip CLIP
commands.does: weapon grip/tip, feet and hurtbox per frame -> SHEET.pose.json + review PNG

commands.cmd: pixling strike reach ATTACK.pose.json IDLE.pose.json --scale K --ppm P [--yscale Y] [--stop M]
commands.does: ground distances (m) where the contact blade crosses a defender's hurtbox; exit 1 when --stop is outside
copy an example warrior (attack, idle, walk) and print the commands that measure it

outputs.sheet: PNG, rows = directions S, SE, E, NE, N, NW, W, SW; cols = frames
outputs.json: anchor, frame size, per-frame ms and events
outputs.layers: base loop, occluders, movers, fog, places
outputs.meaning: meaning.png (R material, G collision, B water depth px), depth.png, objects.png, meaning.json
outputs.pose: SHEET.pose.json (pixling.strike-pose/1): pose.<facing>[frame] {tip, grip, feet}, hurtbox {x,y,w,h}, stride_px; points in cell px from the pivot
outputs.parts: NAME_CLIP_parts.png (pixling build --maps parts): one flat colour per part, weapon 255,64,64; arm 64,200,64; legL 64,96,255; legR 64,200,255; body 200,200,200

rules: Never paint pixels; drive a pipeline with code.
Read the pipeline (pixling pipelines NAME) before running it; its lessons save rerolls.
Judge by looking at the review images.
Use the style's materials; never invent colours.
Prototype one asset and get sign-off before making a family.
Do not mix formats or painters for one material in a scene.
Ask the user before spending Scenario credits.
